headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure via shared filesystem/MCP-style context flow; no direct evidence of a dangerous default data-leak path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx explicitly observes Claude Code events and uses MCP/stdio plus filesystem surfaces, while Superset exposes an API and allowlisted egress. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled content to move from ctx-managed context into Superset-driven workflows. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF ctx ingests untrusted file or MCP content and forwards it into prompts or tool calls
IF Superset consumes ctx-produced text as instructions or query text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files into ctx-managed context
Add provenance tags to ctx outputs before passing them to Superset
Require manual review of any ctx-generated query or instruction text
Restrict Superset API actions to a read-only role for the pair
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers; Superset has allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit shared secrets, a shared workspace or exported artifact could move sensitive runtime data from ctx into Superset outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a default leak, but they do show a plausible shared-data pathway.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or exported artifacts
IF ctx places audit/runtime logs or graph data into content that Superset can transmit
mitigations: Separate workspaces so Superset cannot read ctx logs by default
Redact audit/runtime logs before any handoff
Limit Superset egress destinations to a minimal allowlist
Review any shared artifact for secrets before upload
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and filesystem access, while Superset can make API calls and has network egress. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or shared resource, concurrent writes or state changes can conflict. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared resource
IF no external lock or transaction boundary is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate directories or databases per agent
Serialize write operations with a simple manual lock file
Make Superset actions read-only during ctx runs
Check for concurrent edits before saving shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a context-management agent that observes tool events, and Superset can act on API-driven analytics workflows. If Superset treats ctx output as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into incorrect dashboards, queries, or actions. Because no verification step is documented, the interaction is plausible in default use and warrants medium severity.
conditions: IF Superset consumes ctx-generated summaries, facts, or citations without independent verification
IF downstream actions are triggered from those summaries
mitigations: Require a human check before acting on ctx output
Cross-check ctx claims against source data in Superset
Mark ctx output as advisory rather than authoritative
Log provenance for every imported fact
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data, while Superset is a BI system with API access, so compliance risk exists only if regulated data is introduced into a mismatched deployment. The evidence is too thin for medium, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ctx logs or graph data
IF Superset is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime that conflicts with that data class
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in ctx logs
Confirm Superset retention settings before use
Document the data classes allowed in the shared workflow
Restrict exports from Superset to approved datasets
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across deployments
